name: BALLView
description: WinSparkle Ed25519 pipeline exists but the Windows code never calls win_sparkle_set_eddsa_public_key() — ships live with auto-download+execute and no signature enforcement. Endpoint compromise = RCE (macOS leg inert).
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Windows Sparkle setup registers the appcast URL and initializes WinSparkle, but no public-key registration call appears in this control flow.
limitations: Source-at-commit evidence only; released artifacts and external framework enforcement were not independently verified.

original_evidence.text: | BALLView | https://github.com/BALL-Project/ball.git | 54e7895 / 2026-06-15 | **Y (Windows: live); macOS: present in source but not compiled in for this build state** | Y | Y | https (`https://ball-project.github.io/ball/appcast-{windows,macos}.xml`), TLS validation not disabled anywhere in repo | Appcast items carry `sparkle:edSignature` (Ed25519) placeholders inserted by `scripts/publish_appcast.py` at release time | **Broken on Windows: `win_sparkle_set_eddsa_public_key()` is never called anywhere in the codebase**, so WinSparkle initializes and runs background update checks/downloads with no public key registered — the Ed25519 signature carried in the appcast is never verified. macOS side (`sparkle_bridge.mm`) relies on `SUPublicEDKey` in `Info.plist`, which the release workflow explicitly leaves absent for the current v1.7.0 tag (Sparkle.xcframework isn't vendored in-repo either, so `BALL_HAS_SPARKLE` is OFF for this checkout — macOS auto-update is currently dormant, not shipping) | **none registered at runtime (Windows)** — key is generated/stored as a CI secret and injected only into the appcast signer (`scripts/publish_appcast.py`), never into the client via `win_sparkle_set_eddsa_public_key()` | `source/APPLICATIONS/BALLVIEW/main.C:397-401` (Windows: `win_sparkle_set_appcast_url(...)` + `win_sparkle_init()` called, no key-set call anywhere in file or repo — confirmed via repo-wide grep for `win_sparkle_set_eddsa_public_key`); `vcpkg.json:30` (`winsparkle` is an **unconditional** manifest dependency, so every Windows CI/release build links it — `source/APPLICATIONS/BALLVIEW/CMakeLists.txt:114-129` finds it via `find_package(unofficial-winsparkle CONFIG QUIET)` with no gating); `packaging/appcast/appcast-windows.xml`; macOS gate at `.github/workflows/release.yml:107-155` (explicitly ships v1.7.0 "WITHOUT auto-update infrastructure" when the Ed25519 secret is unset — a real, if slightly saving, guard that Windows lacks) |
